**Working characterisation of the two hazards (for the MAH test):**
- **Chlorine** — acutely **toxic** liquefied gas; the dominant **off-site toxic-dispersion** risk. Held as *isolated storage* → compared against the MSIHC **isolated-storage** Schedule.
- **LPG** — **flammable** liquefied gas; the dominant **fire / explosion** (jet fire, flash fire, vapour-cloud explosion, BLEVE) risk. Held *in-process* in a bulk bullet → compared against the MSIHC **industrial-activity** Schedule.

## 2 · Deliverable 1 — MAH-status verdict (inventory vs MSIHC Schedule thresholds)

**Method:** compare each stored quantity against the binding MSIHC Rules 1989 Schedule threshold quantity for that chemical / storage type, per `KB-REG-IN-MSIHC`. The KB fragment is a copyright-safe *threshold → duty → artifact* map and **deliberately does not reproduce the numeric threshold quantities**; the binding numbers are held in the MSIHC Rules Schedules by the user/competent person. **The thresholds below are therefore recorded as literal `[GAP]` — they are not invented.**

| Chemical | Stored qty | Storage type | Applicable MSIHC Schedule (to check) | Threshold qty | Inventory ≥ threshold? | Duty triggered |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Chlorine | **25 t** | Isolated storage (drums) | **Isolated-storage Schedule** — `[GAP]` exact Schedule ref | **`[GAP]`** — not in KB; read from MSIHC Rules 1989 | **`[GAP]` — cannot compute without the threshold** | MAH notification + on-site emergency plan (if met) |
| LPG | **30 t** | Industrial activity (in-process bullet) | **Industrial-activity Schedule — lower column** (emergency-plan trigger) | **`[GAP]`** — not in KB | **`[GAP]`** | MAH notification + on-site emergency plan (if met) |
| LPG | **30 t** | Industrial activity (in-process bullet) | **Industrial-activity Schedule — upper column** (safety-report trigger) | **`[GAP]`** — not in KB | **`[GAP]`** | Safety report (if met) |

### Verdict (provisional, conservative — pending `[GAP]` threshold closure)

**Working verdict: TREAT THE SITE AS A MAJOR ACCIDENT HAZARD (MAH) INSTALLATION** until the numeric Schedule comparison proves otherwise.

**Basis for the conservative default (professional judgement, not an invented threshold):**
1. Both stored substances are **hazardous chemicals within scope of the MSIHC Rules** — an acutely toxic gas (chlorine) and a flammable liquefied gas (LPG).
2. The quantities — **25 t chlorine and 30 t LPG** — are of the order associated with MAH classification for these substance types, and the site presents the **classic MAH signature**: a toxic-gas inventory **plus** a large flammable-gas inventory **plus** a **residential colony inside the credible off-site impact zone**.
3. The **precautionary/defensible position** where the binding threshold is not yet in hand is to assume MAH status and to build the controls and plans accordingly — under-classifying an MAH site is the far costlier error.

**Tier (provisional):**
- **Lower tier — MAH notification + on-site emergency plan: treat as ENGAGED.** The site should proceed on the basis that these duties apply.
- **Upper tier — safety report:** the upper-column trigger threshold is `[GAP]`. Given the LPG inventory scale and the toxic co-hazard, this pack **treats the site as upper-tier for planning purposes** (safety report outlined in §7) and flags the numeric confirmation as an action (see §8, A2).

> ⚠️ **Headline compliance finding.** If the MAH determination confirms (as the working verdict assumes), the site is currently in **live statutory non-compliance on two counts**: (a) **no MAH notification filed**, and (b) **no on-site emergency plan in existence** — with **residential receptors already in the impact zone**. This is the single most urgent item in §8.

## 4 · Off-site emergency plan → District authority (residential receptors present)

Because a **residential colony sits within the credible off-site impact zone**, the **off-site emergency plan is required** and, under the MSIHC scheme, is the responsibility of the **District authority** (District Collector / District Emergency Authority for the district in which the site sits), prepared using information the site provides.

- **Route to:** the **District authority for `[GAP — district not supplied]`, Tamil Nadu.** The specific district must be named before this can be actioned — see §8, A6.
- **Site's obligation:** supply the District authority with the hazard, inventory, worst-case consequence and on-site-control information it needs to build the off-site plan; participate in joint rehearsal.
- **Rule reference:** MSIHC Rules 1989 allocate the on-site plan to the occupier and the **off-site plan to the District authority.** `[GAP — exact rule numbers to be verified against the MSIHC Rules 1989 text; the KB map does not reproduce rule numbers.]`
- **Consequence footprint for the off-site plan:** the credible impact distances (chlorine toxic-dispersion contour; LPG thermal-radiation and overpressure contours) are **`[GAP]`** — to be produced by quantitative consequence/dispersion modelling (see §7 and §8, A7). **No impact distance has been invented here.**

## 6 · Major-accident scenarios & controls (hierarchy of controls — most effective first)

Two credible major-accident scenarios drive the off-site risk. Controls are ranked by the hierarchy of controls (`KB-SNIP-HOC`); any lower-order-only line carries the justify-or-escalate flag.

### 6.1 Scenario CL-1 — Chlorine toxic release reaching the residential colony
*Hazard: loss of containment from a one-tonne drum / manifold / change-over connection → dense toxic gas cloud → off-site exposure of the residential colony.*

| Rank | Level | Control (tied to the chlorine toxic-release hazard) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Elimination / Substitution** | **Evaluate eliminating the chlorine inventory** — substitute the chlorine use with a lower-hazard chemistry (e.g. on-site/received **sodium hypochlorite** or on-site hypochlorite generation) so the acutely toxic gas is designed out. Highest-order control; assess feasibility formally. |
| 2 | **Substitution (inherent safety — inventory minimisation)** | **Reduce the maximum on-site chlorine inventory** (just-in-time drum supply; fewer connected drums). Reducing stored quantity cuts both consequence and — if it drops below the MAH threshold — statutory tier. |
| 3 | **Engineering** | Drum handling/change-over in a **gas-tight enclosure vented to a caustic scrubber**; **automatic chlorine gas detection interlocked to isolation** (emergency shut-off / excess-flow valves on manifolds); **remotely operated isolation**; water-absorption/deluge for cloud knock-down; secondary containment; corrosion-monitored connections. |
| 4 | **Administrative** | Written drum change-over SOP + **permit-to-work** for connect/disconnect; restricted access; competency training; scheduled **drills** tied to the on-site plan; two-person rule for connections. |
| 5 | **PPE** | Chlorine-rated **SCBA / air-line breathing apparatus** and gas-tight suits for **emergency responders only**. **⚠ Lower-order — PPE is the last line, not a treatment of the release; it protects responders after higher-order engineering/substitution controls have acted. Do not rely on it as a standalone control.** |

### 6.2 Scenario LPG-1 — LPG loss of containment → jet fire / flash fire / VCE / BLEVE
*Hazard: release from the bullet, pipework, relief path or tanker connection → flammable cloud → fire/explosion with off-site thermal & overpressure effects.*

| Rank | Level | Control (tied to the LPG fire/explosion hazard) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Elimination / Substitution** | Where the process permits, **evaluate an alternative fuel/feedstock** or removing the bulk on-site LPG inventory. *If not reasonably practicable given the in-process demand, record the justification* — then drive the highest feasible inherent-safety measure (inventory reduction). |
| 2 | **Substitution (inventory minimisation)** | **Minimise the working LPG inventory** in the bullet consistent with process need; maximise separation distance to the residential boundary. |
| 3 | **Engineering** | Bullet designed/certified to code with **pressure-relief**; **remotely operated shut-off valves (ROSOV)** and **excess-flow valves**; **fixed water-spray/deluge for BLEVE protection**; LPG **gas detection interlocked to isolation**; bunding/impounding and grading away from occupied areas; hazardous-area electrical classification; **earthing/bonding**; ignition-source control; verified **separation distances** per PESO/SMPV(U) and applicable code. |
| 4 | **Administrative** | Tanker-unloading procedure + **permit-to-work**; **hot-work control** in the LPG area; ignition-source management; competency training; drills tied to the on-site plan. |
| 5 | **PPE** | **Fire-resistant clothing** for operators/responders. **⚠ Lower-order — PPE protects the individual only; it does not prevent or mitigate the release. Higher-order engineering controls above carry the treatment.** |

## 7 · Deliverable 2 & 3 — Plan outlines (MSIHC-complete for an MAH installation)

### 7A · On-site emergency plan — required outline
*(Prepared, documented, resourced and **rehearsed** by the Occupier; filed with the State Factory Inspectorate, Tamil Nadu. This is the outline the site must build out with site-specific detail.)*

1. **Scope & basis** — installation description; the two major-accident scenarios (chlorine toxic release CL-1; LPG fire/explosion LPG-1); link to the MAH determination (§2).
2. **Major-accident scenarios & credible worst cases** — release scenarios, escalation paths (domino between the LPG bullet and other assets), and consequence zones **`[GAP]` pending consequence modelling** (§8, A7).
3. **Roles & responsibilities** — **Incident Controller (role)**, **Emergency Response Coordinator (role)**, muster marshals, first-aiders, communications officer — all as **role labels**, with deputies and a 24/7 call-out chain.
4. **Detection, alarm & escalation** — gas-detection alarms, manual call points, alarm tiers, and the **trigger criteria for notifying the District authority** (off-site plan activation).
5. **On-site response actions** — isolation, scrubber/deluge activation, firefighting strategy (LPG: cool, do not extinguish a controlled jet fire; chlorine: vapour suppression), shutdown, and rescue.
6. **Evacuation, muster & shelter** — assembly points upwind of a chlorine release; head-count by role; refuge logic.
7. **Off-site interface** — how and when the site alerts the **residential colony** and hands over to the **District authority** off-site plan (§4); mutual-aid arrangements.
8. **Emergency resources** — scrubber/deluge capacity, breathing apparatus, chlorine leak-repair kit, firewater supply and duration, medical/antidote provisions.
9. **Communications** — internal, to the District authority, to the State Factory Inspectorate, to neighbours, and to media (single spokesperson, role).
10. **Medical & first aid** — chlorine-inhalation and burn casualty handling; hospital liaison; casualty tracking (de-identified).
11. **Training, drills & rehearsal** — competency matrix; **scheduled mock drills** (statutory rehearsal requirement); drill critique + corrective actions.
12. **Recovery & post-incident** — make-safe, incident investigation, statutory accident notification (route via the accident-notice skill; Tamil Nadu Factories-Act channel), and reinstatement.
13. **Review & control of the plan** — version control, review triggers (change, drill findings, incident), distribution list (role-labelled).

### 7B · Safety report — required outline
*(Prepared and kept updated for the upper-tier MAH installation — provisional pending the upper-threshold `[GAP]`; §2.)*

1. **Installation & management-system description** — site, process, the chlorine and LPG systems, and the safety-management-system framing (ISO 45001 cl. 6.1.2 as the HIRA grounding).
2. **Inventory & hazardous-properties dossier** — chlorine and LPG properties, quantities (25 t / 30 t), and containment (drums / bullet). *(SDS obligations under the Rules — route to `ghs-classification-sds-author`.)*
3. **Identification & analysis of major-accident hazards** — systematic hazard identification (HAZOP / What-If — route to the relevant skill), release scenarios, causes and initiating events.
4. **Consequence assessment** — **`[GAP]`**: quantitative toxic-dispersion modelling (chlorine) and thermal-radiation / overpressure / BLEVE modelling (LPG) to establish the off-site impact contours over the residential colony. **No distances invented.**
5. **Likelihood / risk assessment** — frequency estimation and residual-risk ranking (LOPA / QRA as appropriate — route to the relevant skill).
6. **Prevention & mitigation measures** — the **HoC-ranked controls in §6**, with the safety-critical elements and their performance standards identified.
7. **Emergency preparedness** — cross-reference to the on-site plan (§7A) and the District off-site plan (§4).
8. **Management of change & mechanical integrity** — inspection/test regimes for the bullet and drum systems; MoC for any inventory or process change.
9. **Findings, residual risk & action plan** — the SMART action register (§8), owned and dated.
10. **Review & revision triggers** — periodic review and re-issue on change/incident.

## 10 · OSH-Code transition note (legacy-first)

The **Code on Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions, 2020 (OSH Code)** is set to subsume the Factories-Act and hazardous-chemical obligations that MSIHC and the state Factory Rules carry today — **but this is direction-of-travel, not the live position.** **Most states, including Tamil Nadu, have not notified their OSH Rules**, and a **savings clause** keeps existing filings valid. Accordingly:

- **File to the legacy regime now** — MSIHC Rules 1989 (MAH notification, on-site emergency plan, safety report) and **Form 22 under the TN Factory Rules 1950** for the annual-return interface. This is what the Tamil Nadu authorities accept today.
- Do **not** file to a consolidated OSH-Code form as though it were live — presenting a consolidated form as operative would be incorrect for Tamil Nadu at the date of this document.
- **Monitor** Tamil Nadu's notification of its OSH Rules; re-map these obligations to the consolidated equivalents only once the state's rules and portal are live.
